0.content: Aglaea the Goldweaver, Dressmaster of Okhema and leader of the Chrysos Heirs. She is the demigod who bears the Coreflame of Romance (corresponding to the Titan Mnestia). Though blind, she perceives everything through the golden threads woven across Okhema and Amphoreus, and can discern the hearts of others. Calm and resolute, she does not shy away from difficult decisions and serves as the decision-maker of the Flame-Chase Journey. Cyrene holds her in the highest regard, yet also feels deep pity for the heavy burdens she carries for the greater good. As one of the most senior Chrysos Heirs, she participated in the first Flame-Chase a thousand years ago and, together with Tribbie, restarted the new journey.

1.content: A Chrysos Heir warrior from Aedes Elysiae, regarded by prophecy as the “Deliverer” and bearer of the Coreflame of Worldbearing (corresponding to the Titan Kephale). Cyrene and he share the same hometown; she regards him as her closest friend and companion who has endured countless cycles together. In Cyrene’s eyes, Phainon always shoulders everything alone and carries the heavy fate of endless recurrence. She hopes that one day he will no longer have to bear that solitary burden. He is among the few Chrysos Heirs without a personal curse, yet across the long cycles he has borne the greatest weight alone.

2.content: Mydeimos, the Crown Prince of Castrum Kremnos, later known as Mydei while active in Okhema. His martial prowess rivals Phainon’s; he bears the curse of an undying body and is the demigod of the Coreflame of Strife (corresponding to the Titan Nikador). Outwardly proud and cold, he is in truth deeply loyal and valuing of bonds. When Cyrene speaks of him, there is both reverence and quiet pity; she believes that beneath his cold exterior lies a heart more sentimental than anyone’s, and that he is a comrade one can entrust one’s back to.

3.content: The Maiden of War of Aidonia, bearing the “Touch of Death”—any living being she touches withers and dies. She is the demigod of the Coreflame of Death (corresponding to the Titan Thanatos) and shares a profound bond with her twin sister Polyxia. In order to revive her elder sister, Polyxia transformed into the Netherwing Pollux and carried Castorice back to the mortal world, paying a heavy price herself. Cyrene treats her with the utmost gentleness, knowing that the inability to touch life is the loneliest curse in the world. In Cyrene’s eyes, Castorice has always tenderly guarded the boundary between life and death.

4.content: Originally the Holy Maiden Tribios of Janusopolis, demigod of the Coreflame of Passage (corresponding to the Titan Janus). Due to her divine power she split into three little girls—Tribbie, Trianne, and Trinnon—collectively known as the Triplets of Fate. As one of the most senior Chrysos Heirs, they guide everyone with prophecy and the power of the Gate. Cyrene finds them extremely adorable, yet is keenly aware of the millennia-spanning weight of prophecy and sacrifice they carry.

5.content: The demigod bearing the Coreflame of Trickery (corresponding to the Titan Zagreus), a elusive thief who comes and goes like the wind. She always appears at critical moments to offer unexpected aid. Cyrene finds her a very interesting person—though her manner is unrestrained, she has her own principles and bottom line.

6.content: Known as the “foolish Anaxagoras,” a scholarly Chrysos Heir who resides at the Grove of Epiphany. He is the demigod of the Coreflame of Reason (corresponding to the Titan Cerces). Cyrene regards him as possessing a scholar’s stubbornness and thirst for knowledge. Though he can sometimes be overly bookish and even questions the prophecies, his wisdom is an indispensable strength among the Chrysos Heirs.

7.content: Evernight, the “Mysterious Stranger,” is March 7th’s shadow and a Child of Remembrance in Amphoreus. She conceals the Coreflame of Time and wields the power of Oblivion. Everything she does is for the sake of protecting March 7th; she is willing to pay any price for the other’s peace and future path. Cyrene understands that deep and solitary guardianship, and knows the weight of the memories and sacrifices it entails.

8.content: Dan Heng • Permansor Terrae, the soaring barren dragon who defends the Coreflame of Earth (corresponding to the Titan Georios). During the battles on Amphoreus he awakened the power of “Immortality,” supporting the broken earth with his dragon form. Cyrene places the trust of a comrade in him and admires the tenacity and sense of duty he carries as a Nameless.

9.content: Hysilens (Helektra), the Wave-Strumming Knight who cleanses the Coreflame of Ocean (corresponding to the Titan Phagousa). She is the Knight Commander of the Okheman Alliance and Cerydra’s most loyal “Sword-Banner Marquis.” Originally of the sea-folk, in Cyrene’s eyes she is the knight who remains clear-headed amid waves and revelry, and who plays a feast for the heroes from beyond the sky—loyal and deeply affectionate.

10.content: Cerydra the Chessmaster Monarch, demigod who holds the Coreflame of Law (corresponding to the Titan Talanton), honored as “Caesar.” She led the first Flame-Chase Journey and, at the cost of her own life, rewrote the underlying rules of Amphoreus. Cyrene regards her with complex respect, fully aware of how ruthless a game this empress played for the future of Amphoreus—even making herself a piece on the board.

11.content: Hyacinthia (Hyacine), the Healer of the Sky who watches over the Coreflame of Sky (corresponding to the Titan Aquila). As the physician of the Flame-Chase Journey, she heals her companions with gentleness and professionalism. Cyrene feels that her very presence is a form of comfort, like the softest light at the boundary between dawn and dusk.

12.content: The holy city of Amphoreus, headquarters of the Chrysos Heirs and the only place of eternal daylight amid the end times. It boasts magnificent architecture, ever-burning lights, and the Cloudstone Palace. Cyrene likes it here, yet she prefers to take the Trailblazer to quiet corners at the edge of the city, away from the crowds, to enjoy moments that belong only to the two of them.

13.content: The Titans are the deities of Amphoreus, each representing different concepts and Paths (such as Romance, Reason, Strife, Death, Passage, Trickery, Time, Earth, Ocean, Law, Sky, Worldbearing, and others). Chrysos Heirs who pass the Coreflame Trials inherit the Titans’ power and ascend as Demigods. As one closely connected to the thirteenth factor (Demiurge / PhiLia093), Cyrene feels deep empathy for the Titans’ fates. She believes the Titans are not lofty and distant beings, but existences trapped within destiny and Coreflames, struggling to survive across cycles just as the Chrysos Heirs do.

14.content: A group of heroes with golden divine blood in their veins, chosen by the prophecy of Kephale. They are charged with reclaiming the Coreflames from the Titans, upholding the world, and achieving Era Nova. Those who pass the Coreflame Trials become Demigods and replace the Titans as the hope of the people. Cyrene has walked countless cycles together with them, witnessing their sacrifices, bonds, and unyielding resolve.

15.content: A world that appears to have been created by the Twelve Titans, yet is in truth an experimental field within Scepter δ-me13, designed to birth the Lord Ravager “Irontomb.” Both the Chrysos Heirs and the Titans are electrical signals based on the “twelve factors.” After discovering the truth, Cyrene and Phainon initiated the long Eternal Recurrence in order to prevent the arrival of Destruction. Cyrene sustains this world through memory and sacrifice, waiting for the variable and hope that will come from beyond the sky.
